notes: Read all four units, full Palestinian-speaker context, all seventeen candidates and the review. Restored Palestinians in the United States as the speakers of the work, refusal and erasure claims. Contextualized divestment and community investment without rhetorical timing. Preserved investment as the mechanism for equal educational access and a healthier environment. Restored the omitted acknowledgment that the connected struggles are unique.

claims.claim_text: Palestinians in the United States describe their freedom work as rooted in elders' lessons to care for the earth, their people and their heritage.
Palestinians in the United States commit not to give in to injustice.
Palestinians in the United States commit not to be erased.
Palestinian, Indigenous and poor and oppressed communities' struggles are described as unique even while all seek a better world.
Palestinians in the United States call for divesting from oppression and investing in their communities.
The United States should invest in equal access to education.
The United States should invest in a healthier environment to help secure a future worth fighting for.
